cf.title: Temporary slot leak when creation fails in a subtransaction

input.subject: Temporary slot leak when creation fails in a subtransaction

verdict_reasoning: The bug is confirmed in message #2 and the fix changes nothing on disk or in shared memory. The one surviving objection, already-exists-1, is a fixable design point: on HEAD the backend-local variable would sit beside RS_EPHEMERAL, and the author's reason against ephemeral-first creation applies to back branches only. That choice, and a back-patch to 14, need a committer who knows the slot code.

brief.title: Drop a temporary replication slot whose creation fails in a subtransaction
brief.problem: A temporary logical or physical slot whose creation fails inside a subtransaction, with the error caught by a PL/pgSQL exception block, stays until the session ends. A leftover logical slot holds WAL and catalog_xmin, and has no confirmed_flush_lsn, so decoding from it can return a partial transaction. A leftover physical slot holds WAL.
brief.proposed_design: A backend-local variable marks a slot as being created and is reset when the slot is released. If the subtransaction that created a temporary slot aborts with the variable still set, the backend drops the slot instead of releasing it. Nothing changes on disk or in shared memory, so the fix can be back-patched to 14.
user_visible_surface: Behaviour change: a temporary slot is dropped when an error during its creation is caught in a subtransaction.
Documentation of pg_create_physical_replication_slot, pg_create_logical_replication_slot, CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT and the temporary column of pg_replication_slots says so.
author_claims: The bug exists on HEAD and all supported branches back to 14.
The fix is back-patchable and covers both logical and physical temporary slots.
Without the fix, the test shows the leftover slot returning a transaction with one of its two inserts.
Ephemeral-first creation, a new slot state, or a new ReplicationSlot field are invasive or break ABI, so they are not back-patchable.
A resource owner approach does not fit: slots can outlive their (sub)transaction and the walsender creates slots without a transaction.
brief.thread_state: Kuroda confirmed the bug, and shveta malik and Narayanan Venkateswaran plan to review a patch that applies only on top of v19 of another thread's patch. Open: shveta asks whether HEAD should create slots as ephemeral first, keeping the variable for back branches, and the leak of failed persistent physical slots is not yet handled.
unclear: The patch depends on an unmerged patch from another thread, and its order of commit on HEAD and back branches is not stated.
The thread does not settle whether the extra CreateDecodingContext() check on invalid confirmed_flush will be part of the patch.
The patch does not say how it treats a walsender creating a temporary slot outside a transaction.
The patch does not cover failed creation of a persistent physical slot, and no plan for it is agreed.

objections.title: Second "creation in progress" mechanism next to the existing ephemeral state
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a slot creation path, such as a new sync or creation function, and uses only one of the two mechanisms. Nothing fails at once. The leak comes back in that path and is found only when someone hits a caught error during creation.
objections.argument: Postgres already has RS_EPHEMERAL, which drops a persistent logical slot on release if its creation fails. The patch adds MyReplicationSlotCreating for temporary slots, and message #6 proposes extending it to persistent physical slots, so two mechanisms would do the same job on HEAD. The author calls ephemeral-first invasive and not back-patchable, but that argument covers back branches only. In message #7, shveta asks for the ephemeral state on HEAD, and the thread has not settled this.
objections.author_must_show: On HEAD, what stops temporary and physical slots from starting as RS_EPHEMERAL, so that the backend-local variable is needed only on back branches?

critic.reasoning: The author's reason against ephemeral-first creation is that it cannot be back-patched, which does not apply to HEAD. Message #7 asks for ephemeral-first on HEAD and the thread has no answer yet, so the consistency question is open.

refuted.title: HEAD fix differs from the approach the earlier thread preferred
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a new slot creation path on HEAD, such as a new sync or creation variant, without setting the backend-local creation flag. A failed creation in a subtransaction then leaks a temporary slot again. Nothing fails loudly, so users find out only through retained WAL, held catalog_xmin, or partial decoding.
refuted.argument: Message #7 reports the earlier discussion: "Some hackers including me prefer option 1 but we agreed it should be only master as it's impactful." Message #6 still proposes the backend-local flag for HEAD and back branches, and the reason given is the resowner comparison, not ephemeral-first. Ephemeral-first reuses the mechanism persistent logical slots already use, so creation cleanup is part of the slot's state. A flag that each creation path must set and reset is easier to miss in future patches.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should HEAD keep the backend-local flag instead of the ephemeral-first creation that the earlier discussion, as reported in message #7, agreed to prefer on master?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of already-exists-1. Its failure scenario is also weak: the commit message says the variable is set when the slot is created and reset on release, so a new caller of the common creation routine would get it without extra code.

refuted.title: Slot drop in subtransaction abort can fail in the disk-full case
refuted.failure_scenario: A temporary physical slot's state file write fails on a full disk, and a PL/pgSQL block catches the error. The subtransaction abort callback then drops the slot, which renames and fsyncs the slot directory and removes it, on the same full or failing disk. If that step raises an error during abort, the slot may stay half-dropped or the error may escalate.
refuted.argument: Message #1 gives disk exhaustion as the trigger for the physical-slot leak, so the fix runs its file operations under the conditions that caused the first error. Message #2 rejected the resource owner idea because cleanup callbacks must not do work that can fail, and a subtransaction abort callback has the same constraint. Today temporary slots are dropped from top-level error recovery or at process exit, not from inside subtransaction abort. The proposal does not say what happens when the drop itself fails there.
refuted.author_must_show: What happens when dropping the slot from the subtransaction abort callback fails, and is the slot left in a state that error recovery or session exit still cleans up?

critic.reasoning: Dropping a slot renames and removes its directory, which needs no free space, and the existing drop code reports a failed rename of a non-persistent slot as a warning. Top-level error recovery already drops temporary slots under the same disk-full condition.

refuted.title: Second "slot in creation" mechanism next to the existing ephemeral state
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a new slot creation path, such as another synced or temporary slot variant, and sets the ephemeral state but not the backend-local flag. Nothing fails, so a failed creation inside a subtransaction leaks the slot again. Users find out only when WAL or catalog_xmin is held back, or when decoding returns a partial transaction.
refuted.argument: On HEAD the proposal adds a second marker of "creation in progress" beside RS_EPHEMERAL, which persistent logical slots already use for this purpose. Message #6 says the same flag may also cover failed persistent physical slots, so the flag's use is still growing. In message #7, shveta malik prefers ephemeral-first creation on HEAD and notes earlier agreement that such a change belongs only on master. The author's answer that the flag is enough for HEAD and back branches does not address the cost of keeping two mechanisms for one invariant in core for years.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should HEAD keep a backend-local flag instead of using ephemeral-first creation for temporary and physical slots, and what fails loudly when a new creation path forgets the flag?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of already-exists-1, which states the same point about two mechanisms on HEAD more directly.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The patch changes when a temporary replication slot is dropped, in src/backend/replication/slot.c.

touch_points.label: wire protocol
touch_points.reason: protocol.sgml changes the documented behaviour of CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT ... TEMPORARY; no message format changes.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The commit message asks for a back-patch to 14, and the patch applies only on top of an unmerged patch.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: HEAD would carry a backend-local creation variable beside the existing RS_EPHEMERAL state.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: On HEAD, what stops temporary and physical slots from starting as RS_EPHEMERAL, so that the backend-local variable is needed only on back branches?
In which order are this patch and the v19 patch from the other thread to be committed, on HEAD and on each back branch?
Is the CreateDecodingContext() check for an invalid confirmed_flush part of this patch, and on which branches?
How does the patch treat a walsender that creates a temporary slot outside a transaction?
Will the same variable also cover failed creation of a persistent physical slot, or is that a separate patch?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows replication slot lifetime, logical decoding and subtransaction abort handling. The visible messages show reviewers, and no such committer speaking.
committability.liability: A change to slot cleanup during subtransaction abort on six branches, 14 to HEAD, for the life of each branch. A wrong drop or a missed drop holds WAL and catalog_xmin, or lets decoding return a partial transaction.
committability.author_follow_up: The author moved the discussion from the earlier thread and posted a patch with tests and documentation. A rebase was requested in message #3; the visible messages do not show the reply.

priority.reason: The trigger is narrow, a failed temporary slot creation caught in a subtransaction, but the result is retained WAL and partial decoding, and the fix has no cost outside that path. Review needs care in slot.c and postgres.c on six branches, and the patch needs a rebase.

provisional_note: Without the code, two points are unchecked: whether a slot whose creation finished before a later error in the same subtransaction keeps its documented behaviour, and whether walsender slot creation outside a transaction is unaffected. Only 3 of 7 messages were shown.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Error "initial slot snapshot too large" in create replication slot
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes the "initial slot snapshot too large" error in CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT, which happens because SnapBuildInitialSnapshot puts top-level and subtransaction XIDs into the xip array and the count can exceed GetMaxSnapshotXidCount(). Versions tried excluding subtransactions, marking the snapshot takenDuringRecovery, asking the reorder buffer which XIDs are subtransactions, and finally using the subxip array as an extension of xip.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas objected to the last version because it adds a third way of using the xip and subxip arrays, and he saw no consensus on an approach. Earlier approaches failed for other reasons: the reorder buffer cannot reliably tell subtransactions apart, using takenDuringRecovery was rejected, and resizing xip made procarray.c and snapmgr.c too complicated. The author withdrew the entry for lack of a simple fix.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's bad enough that we
already use the xip/subxip arrays in two different ways depending on
the situation. Increasing that to three different ways seems painful.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reuse Workers and Replication Slots during Logical Replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets a tablesync worker, after it finishes one table, pick up the next table in init state and sync it, keeping its replication slot. This removes the cost of starting a new worker and creating and dropping a slot for each table, which matters most for many empty or small tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Benchmarks by reviewers showed regressions in some settings, and the v28 design #2 results were up to about twice as slow as HEAD and varied widely between runs. The patch also no longer applied to HEAD. Amit Kapila proposed Returned with feedback because the regressions still needed analysis, and vignesh C asked for a new entry with a fix for the regression.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IIRC, there were some regressions observed with this patch. So, one
needs to analyze those as well.

precedents_retrieved.title: Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
Reverted commit(s): Track conflict_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Till now, the reason for replication slot invalidation is not tracked
directly in pg_replication_slots. A recent commit 007693f2a3 added
'conflict_reason' to show the reasons for slot conflict/invalidation, but
only for logical slots.

This commit adds a new column 'invalidation_reason' to show invalidation
reasons for both physical and logical slots. And, this commit also turns
'conflict_reason' text column to 'conflicting' boolean column (effectively
reverting commit 007693f2a3). The 'conflicting' column is true for
invalidation reasons 'rows_removed' and 'wal_level_insufficient' because
those make the slot conflict with recovery. When 'conflicting' is true,
one can now look at the new 'invalidation_reason' column for the reason
for the logical slot's conflict with recovery.

The new 'invalidation_reason' column will also be useful to track other
invalidation reasons in the future commit.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add function pg_advance_replication_slot
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a SQL function that moves a physical replication slot forward to a given WAL position without consuming the WAL, for example to keep slots in sync across servers. Later versions named it pg_advance_replication_slot, allowed forward moves only, and raised an error on logical slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier asked that moving the slot backwards raise an error with the current slot position instead of a warning, and that the logical-slot error use ERRCODE_FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED. Andres Freund added that neither message followed the message style guidelines. The patch got no update in the following two months, so it was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
True as well, and the patch did not get an update in two months to
reflect that. So I am marking it as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_replslotdata - a tool for displaying replication slot information
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andres Freund, Michael Paquier, Julien Rouhaud
precedents_retrieved.summary: A new client-side tool, pg_replslotdata, reads the binary replication slot files under pg_replslot/ and prints slot information such as restart LSN, xid, slot type and two-phase state. It works while the server is down, in the same way as pg_controldata and pg_waldump.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Committers judged that the use cases did not justify the cost of maintaining a separate tool in core, including its documentation and translations, and that most needs can be met with an online server. Since the tool is entirely client side, reviewers suggested keeping it in an external repository. The author agreed to drop the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Weighed against the cost of maintaining (including documentation) a separate
tool this doesn't seem sufficient reason.

precedents_retrieved.title: Forbid the use of invalidated physical slots in streaming replication.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes StartReplication() reject a physical replication slot that has already been invalidated, for example by max_slot_wal_keep_size, as the logical walsender already does. Without it a walsender can stream from an invalidated slot, move its restart_lsn forward, and pg_replication_slots shows it as valid while it protects neither WAL nor rows.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding to review questions, so vignesh C moved the entry to Waiting on Author and then to Returned with Feedback. Ashutosh Bapat asked how a build before commit 15f8203 behaves and warned that changing long-released behaviour of physical slots could break backward compatibility. Robert Haas noted that the documentation does not match the current behaviour and that the intended interaction with physical slots is not clear.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think making logical and physical slot behaviour consistent would be
better but if the inconsistent behaviour is out there for some
releases, changing that now will break backward compatibility.

precedents_retrieved.title: enable pg_recvlogical to use temporary slots
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a --temporary-slot option to pg_recvlogical so it can create a temporary logical replication slot that is dropped when the connection ends. In the posted version the option requires --create-slot, takes a slot name, and with --if-not-exists reuses an existing permanent slot of that name.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier asked for a simpler design: --temporary-slot should imply --create-slot, use a PID-based slot name like pg_basebackup, and raise an error when combined with --if-not-exists, --slot or --create-slot. The author did not answer for 8 to 9 weeks, so the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Wouldn't it be
simpler to just error out if combining --temporary-slot and
--if-not-exists altogether?

precedents_retrieved.title: Exit walsender before confirming remote flush in logical replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets a logical replication walsender exit at shutdown without waiting for the subscriber to confirm flush of all sent WAL, so that a publisher with a large time-delayed apply can still stop. Later versions add an optional SHUTDOWN_MODE clause ('wait_flush' or 'immediate') to START_REPLICATION for logical replication.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last shown messages, about a month before the decision, still discuss whether the option should be a boolean or a mode with an explicit default, and they contain minor review comments on v7-0002.

precedents_retrieved.title: Skip replicating the tables specified in except table option
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an EXCEPT TABLE clause to CREATE/ALTER PUBLICATION ... FOR ALL TABLES, which records excluded tables in pg_publication_rel and makes pgoutput skip their changes. A companion patch adds ALTER PUBLICATION ... RESET, which returns a publication to its default state before ALL TABLES with an exception list is added.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch after the thread went quiet. From mid-2022 the messages are rebases and commitfest reminders, and the author said he saw little interest from others. Earlier, Peter Eisentraut doubted the feature was worth the trouble and pointed to the cost of tracking negative dependencies. Peter Smith found the meaning of ALTER PUBLICATION combined with EXCEPT ambiguous, but these points did not decide the outcome.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
As I did not see much interest from others, I'm withdrawing this patch
for now.

precedents_retrieved.summary:

Reverted commit(s): Drop unnamed portal immediately after execution to completion; Add tests for logging of temporary file removal and statement
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 1fd981f05369, based on concerns that the logging
improvements do not justify the protocol breakage of dropping an unnamed
portal once its execution has completed.

It seems unlikely that one would try to send an execute or describe
message after the portal has been used, but if they do such
post-completion messages would not be able to process as the previous
versions.  Let's revert this change for now so as we keep compatibility
and consider a different solution.

The tests added by 76bba033128a track the pre-1fd981f05369 behavior, and
are still valid.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found in the list. The only earlier discussion is the predecessor thread cited in messages #1 and #7, which reports agreement on the bug and a preference for ephemeral-first on master.

The only user-visible change is that a temporary slot whose creation fails inside a caught subtransaction is now dropped. No caller can rely on a half-created slot, and there is no new syntax, GUC, catalog or pg_dump state, so back-patching this does not break any compatibility contract. Two points could not be checked without the code: that a slot whose creation completed before a later error in the same subtransaction keeps its documented behaviour, and that walsender creation outside a transaction is unaffected.

The fix adds no on-disk, WAL, catalog, protocol or ABI change, so pg_upgrade, standbys and extensions are unaffected. The persistent physical slot leak in message #6 is a separate, pre-existing bug and is not counted against this proposal.

The fix has no privilege or exposure aspect. Creating a slot already needs the REPLICATION attribute, and the change only drops the backend's own temporary slot during subtransaction abort, so no role gains new access to data, WAL or other sessions. It also removes a leftover slot that held WAL, so it lowers disk-use risk.
This is a back-patchable bugfix with no hot-path, on-disk or ABI cost. Only the long-run cost of a second creation-state mechanism on HEAD is raised.
This is a bug fix. Postgres has no feature or extension that drops a temporary slot when its creation fails in a caught subtransaction, so only the mechanism duplication applies from this angle.

This is a bug fix: two people reported it, Kuroda confirmed it in message #2, and a test shows a partial transaction being decoded. The trigger is narrow, but the result is WAL and catalog_xmin retention plus data loss, and the cost falls only on the failed-creation path.
